The nightly Rubin stellar screen has 1 target(s) at tier `candidate`: repeated achromatic events at a catalogued position, surviving the flare, dipole, mover and glint cuts and the trial-corrected cross-night test.

Read `results/tocsin/assessment.json` and `watchlist.csv`.

`428209 (2006 VC)` exceeds the radiation momentum ceiling (eps = 1.28) with a reliable orbit solution and is not in the channel's explained set.

A2 = 6.4e-13 au/day^2, S/N 3.8, arc 7139.0 d, diameter 341 m (from H).

Next step is `loom-litcheck --name "428209 (2006 VC)"`: the dark-comet population is incomplete and most exceedances resolve to it.

active.body:
`loom` has advanced from MJD 61344.31881 to MJD 61353.32603 — 9.0 days of sky — after sitting still since 2026-11-02T23:39:18Z.

The stall was confirmed across 7.0 days of sightings; the advance itself happened between 2026-11-09T23:25:47Z and now, so the interval between successive frontier values is 7.0 days. That is an UPPER BOUND on the mirror's true ingest gap — this repository samples the frontier about once a day and cannot see a change finer than that.

The frontier is now 0.7 days behind the wall clock, inside the 30-day limit, so the age alert clears. That is not the same as current: the mirror's ordinary lag is ~16 days, and anything above that is still backlog.

This is the cadence datum `FRONTIER_STALL_DAYS` has never had — it was set to 7 by guesswork because no advance had ever been observed here. Recalibrate it against `observed_advance_days` in `results/alerts/frontier.json` now that there is one.

Note that the nights lost to the stall are ABSENT, not null: they were never observed, so they add nothing to the screen's trial count and must not be counted as clean sky.
active.title: LOOM's data frontier is moving again (+9.0 days of sky)
